title: ESO Guideline 2025: Motor Rehabilitation After Stroke

recommendations.text: Consider adding repetitive upper-limb practice to stroke rehabilitation. The optimal extra dose is unknown but likely ≥20 hours, commonly delivered 3–5 times weekly over 4–6 weeks.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 4, full primary PMC article PMC12098312; PICO 1–6 recommendation and consensus columns; PICO 1; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Only one eligible trial informs this question; no overall recommendation can be made that a particular extra amount of walking practice improves walking capacity after stroke.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 4, full primary PMC article PMC12098312; PICO 1–6 recommendation and consensus columns; PICO 2; recommendation 1

recommendations.section: PICO 2: Additional walking practice in clinical care
recommendations.text: Consider adding walking practice to stroke rehabilitation, preferably ≥20 extra hours. The exact dose is uncertain; available evidence commonly uses 3–5 sessions weekly for 4–6 weeks. Consensus 13/17 members, 76%.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 4, full primary PMC article PMC12098312; PICO 1–6 recommendation and consensus columns; PICO 2; consensus 1

recommendations.text: In chronic stroke with stable cardiovascular status, use high-intensity rather than equal-duration lower-intensity walking training to improve walking endurance.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 4, full primary PMC article PMC12098312; PICO 1–6 recommendation and consensus columns; PICO 3; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: In chronic stroke with stable cardiovascular status, consider high-intensity rather than equal-duration lower-intensity walking training to improve comfortable and maximum walking speed.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 4, full primary PMC article PMC12098312; PICO 1–6 recommendation and consensus columns; PICO 3; recommendation 2

recommendations.text: With only one eligible trial, no overall evidence-based recommendation can be made that adding a behavioural transfer package to equal-duration upper-limb task practice improves activity capacity or performance.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 4, full primary PMC article PMC12098312; PICO 1–6 recommendation and consensus columns; PICO 4; recommendation 1

recommendations.section: PICO 4: Transferring upper-limb gains to daily life
recommendations.text: Consider a transfer package with repetitive task-specific upper-limb training to carry gains into daily life. Components include daily evaluation and a patient diary, problem-solving, a behavioural contract, specified home exercises and weekly follow-up contacts. Consensus 13/17 members, 76%.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 4, full primary PMC article PMC12098312; PICO 1–6 recommendation and consensus columns; PICO 4; consensus 1

recommendations.text: Group-based lower-limb task training may improve activity capacity, with a patient-to-therapist ratio that permits safety and supervision. Provide additional individualised therapy for personal goals and preferences. The PICO compared groups with ≥1:2 therapist-to-patient ratios against time-matched 1:1 training.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 4, full primary PMC article PMC12098312; PICO 1–6 recommendation and consensus columns; PICO 5; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Consider sit-to-stand training in addition to usual care. It needs sufficient repetitions, sessions, duration and appropriate content, but the optimal parameters remain unknown.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 4, full primary PMC article PMC12098312; PICO 1–6 recommendation and consensus columns; PICO 6; recommendation 1
